# Basalt Proxy Code of Conduct

## A welcoming technical community

Basalt Proxy welcomes operators, players, plugin authors, researchers and contributors
of all backgrounds and experience levels. Participation must be respectful regardless
of age, disability, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, nationality, race,
religion, sexual orientation or level of technical knowledge.

This policy applies to this repository's issues, pull requests, reviews and other
project-managed spaces, as well as project-related private messages and conduct
when representing Basalt. It applies to maintainers and contributors alike.

## Expected behavior

- Discuss code and behavior, not a person's worth or motives.
- Give constructive, specific feedback and accept good-faith corrections.
- Respect different levels of experience and allow people time to respond.
- Keep reports reproducible and discussions relevant. Disagreement about vanilla
  parity, protocol behavior or plugin compatibility is welcome; personal attacks are not.
- Protect private information in logs, configurations, screenshots and reports.
- Respect moderation decisions and requests to stop disruptive behavior.

Harassment, discriminatory abuse, sexual harassment, threats, doxxing, stalking,
impersonation, spam and persistent hostile disruption are not acceptable. Do not
publish someone else's personal information or private communications without permission.
Retaliation against a reporter or someone assisting a report is also unacceptable.

## Reporting concerns

Report project-related conduct concerns privately to
[hello@basaltmc.org](mailto:hello@basaltmc.org). Put **Basalt Proxy conduct report** in
the subject and include links, relevant context and the safest way to contact you.
Do not open a public issue containing private evidence or identifying information.

If a concern involves a maintainer, state that clearly so another available
maintainer can review it. You can also use
[GitHub's abuse reporting process](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/acceptable-use-policies/github-community-guidelines#reporting-abuse).
This policy does not replace emergency services or GitHub's own platform rules.

Security vulnerabilities belong in the [private security reporting process](https://github.com/BasaltProject/Proxy/blob/main/SECURITY.md),
not public conduct discussions or ordinary bug reports.

## Enforcement

Maintainers review reports in context and may request more information. Information
is shared only as needed to assess and address a report; absolute confidentiality
cannot be guaranteed. Reporters' privacy and safety should guide how evidence is handled.

Depending on severity and repeated behavior, responses can include a request to
correct behavior, a warning, removal of content, or temporary or permanent limits
on participation in project-managed spaces. Serious threats or abuse may be referred
to GitHub. A maintainer directly involved in a complaint should not decide its outcome alone.

To request a review of a moderation decision, use the same private contact and explain
what should be reconsidered. Do not use public threads to harass participants or evade restrictions.
